title: Execute replaceable linked semantics and strengthen verification
body:
## Status

This PR advances #183 and remains in progress. The exhaustive requirements ledger and the execution-backed acceptance manifest under `docs/case-studies/issue-183/` retain every open requirement. Full production-language semantics, complete native RML replay of the upstream corpus, multiple genuinely different minimal foundations, and full Link-driven implementation closure remain unfinished.

## Latest implementation and verification

- Per-registry linked K0 artifacts can be replaced without rebuilding either runtime or affecting another registry. The shared recursive-substitution witness changes nested output from the selected linked definition. The host compiler and S/K equations remain explicit boundaries.
- An independent direct-lambda control executes the authoritative linked source without bracket compilation and observes the same reductions and proof trees. Its five external machine transitions are explicit; it is not counted as a genuinely different minimal foundation.
- The registered RML syntax extension supports source-free canonical emission and interoperable snapshots, with rejection of dangling, cyclic, malformed or exponentially expanding syntax networks. Conservative identifier rewriting preserves shadowing and refuses capture and unsupported scopes.
- Concurrent named/versioned packages receive private program addresses and explicit imports. Query and refutation are checked independently, and results retain the selected foundation, assumptions, cycle policy and bounds.
- Links-defined probability/confidence policies carry dependencies and explicit independence assumptions. Mutation tests cover evidence and policy invalidation.
- The public linked proof verifier independently checks finite inductive proof certificates from caller-selected rules, context and goal. Shared adversarial cases, exact replay, definition replacement, primitive removal and bounded input handling are tested in both runtimes. It does not elaborate the entire upstream proof corpus.
- Strict typed-link archives preserve addresses, sharing, cycles and Unicode while rejecting identity collisions and dangling data. Explicit linked universe-policy witnesses keep a network self-reference separate from a logical `Type : Type` judgement.
- All 12 directed JavaScript/Rust/Lean/Rocq translations are implemented for the documented pure-natural-function fragment. All 96 native observations pass, and three false Rocq observations are rejected. Unsupported production-language constructs retain their source and precise obligations; full-language coverage remains required.
- Repository-owned cache cleanup has installed composed hooks, command lifecycle wrappers, CI teardown, budgets and protected source/evidence handling. Namespace-aware leases and owned Docker teardown fail closed. Measured clean/rebuild cycles and remaining portability/accounting boundaries are recorded.
- The always-selected complete-delivery job checks live requirement-source freshness, pinned implementation/fixtures and actual positive/negative assertion execution. Passing smaller progress witnesses cannot certify a broader requirement.

Evidence and scope:
- `docs/case-studies/issue-183/runtime-kernel-replacement.md`
- `docs/case-studies/issue-183/meta-language-integration.md`
- `docs/FOUNDATION_PACKAGES.md`, `docs/FOUNDATION_WORKSPACE.md`
- `docs/LINKED_PROOF_VERIFICATION.md`, `docs/SEMANTIC_ARCHIVE.md`
- `docs/case-studies/issue-183/portable-natural-translation.md`
- `docs/BUILD_CACHE.md` and `docs/case-studies/issue-183/data/`

The published `fddfba1` checkpoint passed all seven ordinary CI workflows. Subsequent focused verification includes the complete linked proof witness and native four-language observation matrix; the complete-delivery gate remains failing while requirements are unmet.

## What changed

### Replacing a linked definition of K1 (R150 partial, R149 and R151 open)

Review `5836717056` asks for an executable witness that the semantics comes from linked definitions: run D on an unchanged generic runtime, replace D with D′, and get execution according to D′. The mirrored `executes a replaced linked definition of K1 on the unchanged runtime` tests in `js/tests/linked-program.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/linked_program_tests.rs` replace one rule of `links-meta-foundation` in `lib/meta-theory/universal.lino` at a time and run the same request through the same runtime:

| Mechanism (rule replaced) | Under D | Under D′ |
|---|---|---|
| matching (`match-repeated-variable`) | `(pair (atom a) (atom b))` | `(atom same)` |
| substitution (`substitute-pair`, mirrored) | `(pair (atom a) (atom done))` | `(pair (atom done) (atom a))` |
| rule selection (`select-next-object-rule`) | `(atom second)` | `(atom a)` |
| verification (`verify-object-result`) | `verified` | `(verified (atom a))` |

In every case the replaced rule fires, and the host operations under D and D′ are the same four: `contract-k-link`, `contract-s-link`, `enforce-cycle-and-resource-bounds`, and `parse-linked-forms`. The runtime sources and the compiled `fixed-point.ski` never name the constructors those rules use (`meta-substitute`, `finish-meta-apply`, `select-meta-rewrite`, `rewrite-miss`, `binding-found`, `match-ok`), so no host branch decides what the replaced definitions do. `experiments/definition-replacement/k1-replacement.mjs` prints the same comparison.

Changing only K1 still leaves K0 unchanged. The later runtime K0 replacement witness now loads a different compiled Links artifact into one registry without changing the runtime or another registry. It changes recursive substitution itself; the host compiler still compiles both linked definitions. R150 retains its broader recursive mechanism gap.

The review's acceptance gate is registered as R149 (Open): at least two different minimal meta-foundations, each showing closure, substitutability, semantic preservation, minimality relative to the witness, no hidden host authority, self-interpretation, and a complete trust boundary. The S/K `6/6` witness is recorded as the current implementation bootstrap, not completion, and one reduced foundation has no comparable peer. R151 (Open) records that the parser, elaborator, compiler, and code generation are still host code, so full implementation closure has not been reached.

### One LiNo front end for both runtimes

Both runtimes now read every `.lino` document through one front end, `js/src/rml-lino-frontend.mjs` and its Rust mirror `rust/src/lino_frontend.rs`, instead of calling `links-notation` 0.20 directly. The front end:

- reads every reference that opens with a quote itself, in one left-to-right pass, and hands the parser a token in its place;
- hands the parser no piece whose parentheses nest more than two levels deep (`LINO_PIECE_DEPTH`), putting a one-name placeholder where a deeper group stood;
- refuses a document nested deeper than 64 parenthesis-and-indentation levels (`MAX_LINO_NESTING_DEPTH`) or longer than `MAX_LINO_SOURCE_UNITS` code units, with the parse error `E006`;
- builds the links of an indented id itself: a line under an indented id keeps its name, and an indented id among those lines reads the way it reads on its own, so `a:` over `b: c` reads as `(a: (b: c))`; a line indented under any other line of an indented id is refused with `E006` instead of being dropped.

`js/tests/lino-frontend.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/lino_frontend_tests.rs` check the same 100 cases in `test-corpus/lino-frontend/cases.json`, read 64 indented ids nested one under another and refuse 65, read twelve sources built to be slow within five seconds each, and keep references made of private-use characters apart from the names the front end makes. `experiments/lino-frontend/differential.mjs`, `deep-documents.mjs`, `quote-reading.mjs`, and `nested-indented-ids.mjs` compare the two front ends over generated documents and find no difference.

### Upstream links-notation reports

Reading `links-notation` 0.20 directly on these shapes is why the front end exists. `experiments/lino-frontend/upstream.mjs` shows, in both runtimes, what the parser reads alone and how long it takes. The findings are filed against `link-foundation/links-notation`:

- #312 - the JavaScript and Rust parsers disagree on a lone CR, Unicode spaces, a last line of spaces, and singlets;
- #313 - lines under an indented id lose their names and their own indented lines;
- #314 - reading nested groups takes time that grows exponentially with the nesting in both ports, and the Rust `parse_lino_to_links` entry point adds quadratic time by deep-copying the subtree once per level;
- #315 - a deeply nested document overflows the Rust stack and aborts the process uncatchably, and neither port enforces the nesting-depth limit it documents;
- #316 - reading a reference that opens with a wide run of quotes takes quadratic time in both ports.

The three denial-of-service reports, #314 through #316, were filed after the maintainer authorized public reporting (PR comments 5831221597 and 5831357798). The front end already caps source size and nesting depth and reads quoted references itself, so both runtimes stay away from these shapes.

### Selectable type ontology (R129 complete, R114 partial)

`recursive-type-ontology.md` and the mirrored `linkCliInteropProfile` / `link_cli_interop_profile` tests classify the opt-in link-cli type ontology as a candidate default construction, not a premise about what links intrinsically are or a logical `Type : Type` rule (R129, complete). The default is available only through an explicit factory; the mirrored `leaves the default type ontology to the callers that select it` tests find no `Type` link in a bare typed network, no runtime module that selects the default ontology, and an evaluator whose universes stay stratified, answering `Type of Type` only for a source that declares `(Type: Type Type)`. Foundation-declared universe and soundness contracts remain open (R114, partial).

### Foundational orientation audit (R148)

Review `5823272578` is registered as R148 (Partial), with the "Where consequence orientation can come from" section added to `foundation-search.md`. The mirrored `orientationAudit` / `orientation_audit` tests ask where the orientation of a consequence could come from without assuming source/target, premise/conclusion, time, rewrite direction, function/argument, cause/effect, truth, or proof, and separate intrinsic asymmetries from observer-chosen ones across automorphism-distinguished structures, same-observation pairs, renaming, faithful representations, and carrier recursion. The result is a finite no-go, `CONSEQUENCE_ORIENTATION_DISTINGUISHED_BUT_NOT_FORCED`: address equality and slot order separate the two candidate orientations but never rank them, because composing any invariant selector with the output swap gives an invariant selector that chooses the opposite orientation. R147 stays Partial; an intrinsic orientation of consequence remains open.

### PR metadata

The description ends with `Advances #183` and names no issue in a closing directive, because #183 is not complete. A step in `tests.yml` runs on every PR 184 event, reads the live description through the API, and removes any whole-line closing directive in every GitHub form (`#N`, `owner/repo#N`, or the issue URL, with an optional colon and trailing period), writing only when something changed and failing if a directive appears inside other text. Its tests cover the updated, unchanged, inline-refusal, and other-PR paths.

## Earlier verification before the latest implementation

- `node --test scripts/foundation-search.test.mjs scripts/issue-183-requirements.test.mjs`
- `npm test` in `js/` (1506 passed)
- `cargo test --all-targets` in `rust/` (942 passed)
- `npm run lint:english`, `npm run test:bootstrap`, `npm run report:bootstrap-metrics`, and `npm run report:foundation-search` in `js/`

The finite no-go covers address equality and slot order under the named, anonymous, and unordered contracts and adds no direction bit; it does not exclude a more primitive Links property outside those observations. A host-free generic principle that derives a consequence from its premises, an intrinsic continuation law, implication, execution, and law-level self-application all remain open.

Advances #183
